pages.title: Does restaurant bookkeeping include taxes?
pages.heading: Does restaurant bookkeeping include taxes?
pages.description: Understand the difference between restaurant bookkeeping, tax preparation and filing. Confirm what the agreement includes and who is responsible.
pages.eyebrow: Restaurant finance answer / Bookkeeping and taxes
pages.answer: Bookkeeping does not automatically include tax preparation, filing or advice. Those tasks must be expressly included in the agreement, with the responsible provider identified.

sections.title: Bookkeeping prepares the accounting records
sections.body: Transaction entries, reconciliations and supporting documents help a tax professional prepare their work. Completing the books does not establish that a return was prepared or filed.

sections.title: Ask for the tax responsibilities in writing
sections.body: Confirm the taxes covered, preparer, reviewer, authorized payer and submitting person. Ready Margin can organize agreed records and coordinate the handoff; specialist work is separately confirmed.

resources.label: IRS — Employer responsibilities when outsourcing payroll

pages.title: Who handles restaurant payroll taxes?
pages.heading: Who handles restaurant payroll taxes?
pages.description: Check the employer, payroll processor and adviser responsibilities for payroll-tax work. Name the preparer, approver and submitting provider in the agreement.
pages.answer: The restaurant, its payroll processor and any appointed adviser divide payroll-tax tasks according to their agreements and applicable requirements. Confirm who calculates, files and pays; payroll preparation alone does not prove those tasks were completed.

sections.title: Follow the task through to submission
sections.body: Identify the provider responsible for each return and payment, the authorizing person and the evidence of completion. Confirm responsibilities with that provider rather than assuming every payroll service covers them.

sections.title: Separate record preparation from tax processing
sections.body: Ready Margin’s agreed preparation work can organize hours, tips, corrections and payroll records. The engagement separately confirms payroll processing, tax tasks and any specialist advice.

pages.title: When does a restaurant need a fractional CFO?
pages.seoTitle: When does a restaurant need a fractional CFO?
pages.heading: When does a restaurant need a fractional CFO?
pages.description: Recognize when restaurant decisions need CFO support: cash planning, expansion analysis or interpretation of recurring financial results.
pages.answer: Fractional CFO support can be useful when an owner needs financial planning and decision support beyond keeping the accounts current. Examples include cash planning, expansion analysis and regular review of performance changes.
queries: when does restaurant need fractional CFO
does my restaurant need a CFO

sections.title: Identify the decision requiring financial planning
sections.body: State what you need to decide and when. An equipment purchase, new location and ongoing margin review need different analysis and meeting frequency.

sections.title: Check whether the records can support the review
sections.body: Current accounts and identified cash commitments are needed for useful analysis. If the books are behind, the first engagement may need to address those records before a forecast or scenario review.

related.label: Restaurant bookkeeper, CPA or fractional CFO?

pages.title: How should a restaurant cash-flow review start?
pages.seoTitle: How should a restaurant cash-flow review start?
pages.heading: How should a restaurant cash-flow review start?
pages.description: Start a restaurant cash-flow review with a dated balance, settlement dates and payment obligations. Separate confirmed amounts from assumptions.
pages.answer: Start by dating the bank balances and listing receipts expected and payments due over the same period. Check settlement timing and identify uncertain amounts before deciding what cash is available.
queries: how to fix restaurant cash flow
restaurant running out of cash what to do

sections.title: Build the payment timeline
sections.body: Include payroll, approved supplier bills, rent and other known commitments. Record the date, amount and authorizing person for each relevant decision.

sections.title: Verify the receipts and update the plan
sections.body: Use card and delivery settlement statements to check what should arrive and when. Ready Margin can help investigate gaps and prepare scenarios; the response depends on the cause and may require specialist advice.

pages.title: How can a restaurant investigate high food cost?
pages.seoTitle: How can a restaurant investigate high food cost?
pages.heading: How can a restaurant investigate high food cost?
pages.description: Check supplier prices, stock timing, portions and sales mix to understand high restaurant food cost. Choose changes based on the evidence.
pages.answer: Check whether the change comes from supplier prices, stock timing, usage, portions or sales mix. Compare the same period and units before choosing a purchasing or kitchen change.
queries: how to reduce restaurant food cost

sections.title: Confirm prices and quantities
sections.body: Match invoices to pack sizes and receiving records. A changed case size can look like a price increase until you compare cost per usable unit.

sections.title: Check recipes and counts with the kitchen
sections.body: Use current recipe quantities, usable yields, portions and count dates. Ready Margin can investigate the agreed records; management selects the change and measures its effect.

pages.title: How can a restaurant review labor cost?
pages.seoTitle: How can a restaurant review labor cost?
pages.heading: How can a restaurant review labor cost?
pages.description: Review restaurant labor cost with comparable sales, schedules, attendance and payroll inputs. Keep staffing decisions grounded in operating requirements.
pages.answer: Use sales and full employment costs for the same period, then compare planned shifts with recorded hours. Confirm unusual time entries and operating changes before deciding on staffing.
queries: how to control restaurant labor cost

sections.title: Define the cost being compared
sections.body: Scheduled base wages do not include every employment cost. Agree the treatment of payroll taxes, benefits and other costs, then use consistent periods.

sections.title: Bring managers into the explanation
sections.body: Cover shifts, training and service requirements may explain additional hours. Ready Margin can review the financial effect; managers retain staffing and pay decisions.

resources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

pages.title: What is restaurant back-office support?
pages.heading: What is restaurant back-office support?
pages.description: Learn which restaurant finance jobs back-office support can cover, from bookkeeping and payroll inputs to invoice collection and review coordination.
pages.answer: Restaurant back-office support covers agreed administrative and finance tasks such as bookkeeping, payroll preparation, supplier-bill records and coordination between managers and advisers. The scope varies by provider.
queries: what is restaurant back office support
what does restaurant back office do

sections.title: Ask for named tasks and outputs
sections.body: Confirm who collects statements, reconciles accounts, checks attendance and prepares the review. Broad labels do not establish which jobs will be completed.

sections.title: Confirm the boundaries
sections.body: The restaurant supplies operating facts and retains defined approvals. HR, tax, legal work and payment execution require explicit arrangements rather than being assumed part of general support.

pages.title: What is managed restaurant finance?
pages.heading: What is managed restaurant finance?
pages.description: Understand how a managed restaurant finance service combines recurring work and review. Compare the people, deliverables and approvals included.
pages.answer: Managed restaurant finance is a service in which a team handles defined finance tasks and reviews the results with the restaurant. The scope may combine bookkeeping, accounting, payroll preparation and financial guidance.

sections.title: Evaluate the delivery responsibility
sections.body: Ask who completes the work, what records they need, when reports arrive and how unresolved questions are followed up. A workspace can organize that work; the service agreement establishes responsibility.

sections.title: Choose the support your restaurant needs
sections.body: Ready Margin quotes around your locations, systems and selected tasks after a free demo. The proposal identifies deliverables, fees, restaurant approvals and separately appointed specialists.

pages.title: Can one team handle restaurant payroll and bookkeeping?
pages.seoTitle: Can One Team Handle Payroll & Bookkeeping?
pages.heading: Can one team handle restaurant payroll and bookkeeping?
pages.description: See how payroll preparation and restaurant bookkeeping can share records while retaining separate cutoffs, checks and approvals.
pages.eyebrow: Restaurant finance answer / Payroll and books
pages.answer: One team can handle payroll preparation and bookkeeping if the agreement covers both. Payroll still needs its own approval cutoff, and the accounts need their own reconciliation and close checks.
queries: who can handle payroll and bookkeeping for my restaurant

sections.title: Connect the records without merging the approvals
sections.body: Approved payroll reports can support accounting entries and labor analysis. Time and tip inputs must be checked before payroll; account reconciliation checks a different part of the process.

sections.title: Confirm processor and tax responsibilities
sections.body: Ready Margin can quote for both preparation and bookkeeping. The engagement separately identifies the payroll processor, tax work and restaurant authorization.

pages.title: Is Ready Margin software or a managed service?
pages.seoTitle: Is Ready Margin software or a managed service?
pages.heading: Is Ready Margin software or a managed service?
pages.description: Ready Margin provides managed restaurant finance support. Learn how the workspace supports the team and what the public demonstration shows.
pages.answer: Ready Margin is a managed restaurant finance service supported by a workspace. Our team handles the tasks named in your agreement. The public workspace demonstrates review processes with sample records.

sections.title: The service defines the work we handle
sections.body: Your proposal names the preparation, checks and financial reviews included, along with the records your team supplies and the approvals it keeps.

sections.title: The demo shows the workflow
sections.body: The public views illustrate attendance, tips, payroll preparation, bills, reconciliation and cash review. Sample balances and entries are not your restaurant’s live data. Provider connections and payroll processing are confirmed separately.
